preamble: No verified case of /ʂ/ > /θ/ has been found. The previously cited Castilian Spanish development is misassigned: Castilian /θ/ comes from the medieval dental affricates /t͡s/ (ç, c) and /d͡z/ (z), which deaffricated to dental /s̪/ and then fronted to interdental /θ/. The Old Spanish apico-alveolar /s̺/, sometimes described as retracted, did not become /θ/; it survives as Castilian /s/. The Castilian change belongs to the ts_to_th_vless cell.

examples.note: The source of /θ/ is the dental affricate /t͡s/, not a retroflex /ʂ/

sources: Penny, R. (2002). A History of the Spanish Language (2nd ed.). Cambridge University Press. https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511992827
